authority: This catalogue owns component-selection metadata. Component guides own syntax and semantics.json owns authored semantics.

components.title: App bar
jobs: Material Design 3 Expressive app bars: small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search, from the HTML.
useWhen: Page title and screen-level actions.
avoidWhen: Peer destinations need navigation; categories need tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search app bars.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native header/nav composition; AppBar owns scroll collapse and search expansion.

components.selectionExample: A Home/Search/Profile row belongs in navigation, even if placed at the top. Keep the app bar for the title and screen actions.

components.title: Bottom app bar
jobs: This screen's commands at the bottom edge, with an optional FAB — not its destinations.
useWhen: This screen's commands at the bottom edge, with an optional FAB — not its destinations.
avoidWhen: The items are destinations rather than commands, or a top toolbar fits the task.

implementation.documentedSupport: Bottom command bar with optional FAB.
implementation.webAdaptation: Tab-reachable commands; no toolbar composite role.
limitations: Retained API; use a docked toolbar for new M3 Expressive work when its behavior fits.

upstreamReview.note: Google MDC Android marks bottom app bar available but deprecated/not recommended in M3 Expressive; docked toolbar replaces it. Legacy M2 link observed: https://m2.material.io/components/app-bars-bottom .

materialGuidance.reason: Legacy Material component; Google deprecates it for M3 Expressive in favor of docked toolbars.

components.title: Navigation bar
jobs: Switch between UI views on compact and medium screens.
useWhen: Persistent peer destinations on compact screens.
avoidWhen: Commands need buttons; local panels need tabs.

adaptive.reason: Use persistent peer navigation at wider widths.
Use a drawer when nested destinations need more space.

implementation.documentedSupport: Stacked and horizontal destination layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links navigate; the application marks the current destination.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity within an account page should not displace Home/Search/Profile in app navigation. Use tabs for those local panels and preserve the app destinations across widths.

components.title: Navigation rail
jobs: Switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.
useWhen: Switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.
avoidWhen: Destinations are nested or the surface is Compact.

adaptive.reason: Compact peer destinations fit the bottom edge.
Use the expanded rail when labels should remain visible.
Use a drawer when nested destinations need more space.

implementation.documentedSupport: Collapsed, expanded, and modal rails.
implementation.webAdaptation: The compact expanded rail uses a scrim and dismissal behavior.

upstreamReview.note: tab observed; destination not followed; link-observed; full specifications not reviewed

components.title: Navigation drawer
jobs: A slide-out menu, or a fixed sidebar on Expanded and wider screens.
useWhen: A slide-out menu, or a fixed sidebar on Expanded and wider screens.
avoidWhen: Flat peer destinations fit a bar or rail, or the content is details for the current item.

adaptive.reason: Use a modal drawer when destinations overflow compact navigation.
Use a fixed drawer when nested destinations need persistence.

implementation.documentedSupport: Sliding and fixed drawers with nested sections.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native details/summary supports nesting.
limitations: Retained baseline navigation component; current Expressive guidance points to expanded navigation rail as its replacement.

components.title: Panes
jobs: Material 3 canonical layouts, from the HTML.
useWhen: Responsive list-detail or supporting layouts.
avoidWhen: A single collection needs a list, not multiple panes.

adaptive.reason: Stack or collapse panes when their container cannot preserve useful pane widths.

implementation.documentedSupport: List-detail, supporting pane, and equal panes.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS viewport and container queries; the application chooses the active compact pane.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered canonical examples overview reviewed: feed, list-detail, supporting pane; equal and three-pane framework variants are not verified upstream specifications.

materialGuidance.reason: Canonical layout pattern, not a standalone component.

components.selectionExample: A contact directory with no detail view needs a list. Use list-detail panes when selecting a contact reveals a separate detail region.

components.title: Footer
jobs: Site navigation and extra information at the end of a page.
useWhen: Site links and legal information at page end.
avoidWhen: Primary app destinations need persistent navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Native footer with navigation columns and copyright content.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web page landmark styled with theme roles.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile should not require scrolling to a footer. Use a navigation bar or rail for those destinations.

components.title: Tabs
jobs: Material Design 3 tabs, from the HTML.
useWhen: Switch related content panels within one page.
avoidWhen: App destinations need navigation; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Primary and secondary tabs; stacked and horizontal icon layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links target panels; use the shipped runtime keyboard contract.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile are app destinations, so use a navigation bar or rail. Overview/Activity panels within one account page can use tabs; Day/Week/Month as a view setting can use segmented inputs.

components.title: Breadcrumbs
jobs: The path to this page, from the HTML.
useWhen: Ancestor path to the current page.
avoidWhen: Peer views need tabs; numbered results need pagination.

implementation.documentedSupport: Breadcrumb links and app-bar composition.
implementation.webAdaptation: Labelled navigation with an ordered list and current-page link.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity/Billing are peers, not ancestors. Use tabs for their same-page panels, not a breadcrumb trail.

components.title: Pagination
jobs: A list of pages. The HTML is the component.
useWhen: Move through pages of one result set.
avoidWhen: In-page sections need anchors or scrollspy.

implementation.documentedSupport: Page links, active page, and unavailable previous/next items.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only navigation; the application supplies destinations.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A long article with Introduction/Methods/Results needs section links, optionally with scrollspy, not numbered result pages.

components.title: Menu
jobs: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The choices need persistent layout space, blocking interaction, or peer navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Vertical menus, nested flyouts, grouping, and standard/vibrant styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native menu/li structure; Menu owns opening and keyboard behavior.

components.title: Scrollspy
jobs: Highlight the table of contents as the page scrolls.
useWhen: Track visible sections in a table of contents.
avoidWhen: Separate views need navigation or tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Section tracking and table-of-contents links.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web document navigation helper.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A settings screen with mutually exclusive panels needs tabs. Scrollspy only tracks sections already present in the scrolling document.

components.title: Buttons
jobs: Material Design 3 common buttons, icon buttons, and FABs — from the HTML.
useWhen: Run an action with a visible label.
avoidWhen: Stored choices need inputs; destinations need links.

implementation.documentedSupport: Filled, tonal, outlined, elevated, and text; xsmall through xlarge.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native buttons run commands; a.button links navigate.
limitations: Standalone common buttons do not document a square/toggle shape-morph contract; do not borrow icon-button or connected-group modifiers.

upstreamReview.note: rendered main content reviewed in part; link-observed; full specifications not reviewed

components.selectionExample: A saved delivery-speed choice needs radios or segmented inputs, not three action buttons.

components.title: Icon buttons
jobs: A single icon as the whole control, in four styles and five sizes.
useWhen: Compact actions with recognizable icons.
avoidWhen: An unfamiliar action needs a visible button label.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard, filled, tonal, outlined; five sizes; narrow, wide, and square.
implementation.webAdaptation: Accessible name belongs to the control; the glyph is decorative.
limitations: Elevated and text are not icon-button variants.

components.selectionExample: A novel approval workflow should use a labeled button. A tooltip on an ambiguous icon cannot replace a clear label or the control's accessible name.

components.title: Segmented buttons
jobs: Two to five connected options, one choice or several, with no script behind them.
useWhen: Choose 2–5 values using native radio/checkbox inputs.
avoidWhen: Independent commands need a standard button group.

implementation.documentedSupport: Single-select radio and multi-select checkbox groups.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native fieldset/input/label owns selection and form values.
limitations: The selected check icon is authored; the framework does not insert it.

components.selectionExample: Cut/Copy/Paste are commands, not stored choices. Use a standard button group. A shipping-speed value submitted with a form fits single-select segmented inputs with one shared radio name.

components.title: Button groups
jobs: Related action or toggle buttons that grow and reshape together, in two variants and five sizes.
useWhen: Cluster commands or aria-pressed toggle buttons.
avoidWhen: Submitted values need segmented or other native inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and connected groups; commands and opt-in selection.
implementation.webAdaptation: Runtime coordinates neighboring widths and selection; CSS handles connected shapes.

components.selectionExample: Economy/Express delivery submitted on Save needs radios or segmented inputs. Standard groups fit Cut/Copy/Paste; connected groups fit toggle states, not one-shot commands. A pressed button does not submit a radio value.

components.title: Split button
jobs: A lead action and a trailing half that opens a menu of related ones, in five sizes.
useWhen: Default action plus related menu actions.
avoidWhen: Equal actions need a group; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Leading action and trailing menu trigger with matching styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Reuses Menu; no separate split-button runtime.

components.selectionExample: PDF/CSV format selection for a later Export action belongs in a select or segmented inputs. A split button fits Export now plus alternate export commands.

components.title: Floating action button
jobs: A circular action that can open a menu of related shortcuts.
useWhen: A circular action that can open a menu of related shortcuts.
avoidWhen: The action is not the single highest-priority screen action.

adaptive.reason: Use the extended FAB when the action benefits from a visible label.

implementation.documentedSupport: FAB sizes, extended FABs, and menus of related actions.
implementation.webAdaptation: Floating action behavior uses the documented FAB runtime.

components.title: Cards
jobs: Material Design 3 cards, from the HTML.
useWhen: Distinct items with their own content or actions.
avoidWhen: Dense comparable rows need a list.

implementation.documentedSupport: Elevated, filled, outlined, horizontal, and directly actionable cards.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native article anatomy; primary-action links preserve navigation semantics.

components.selectionExample: A hundred compact activity records need a list. Giving every row a card adds separation without a separate content or action group.

components.title: Lists
jobs: Continuous vertical indexes of text and images.
useWhen: Scan repeated rows of text and images.
avoidWhen: Rich independent items need cards.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and segmented lists.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native list semantics; visual selection alone does not justify aria-selected.

components.selectionExample: A product with a large image, description, price, and several actions may need a card. A simple product-name index remains a list.

components.title: Dialogs
jobs: Important prompts in a user flow. Dedicated to a single task.
useWhen: Focused prompts or decisions that interrupt the flow.
avoidWhen: Ignorable feedback needs snackbar or banner.

implementation.documentedSupport: Basic and full-screen dialogs.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.showModal()/close(); shared dialog behavior is separate from AutoInit.

components.selectionExample: Saving successfully should not force dismissal of a dialog. Use a snackbar for that feedback and a banner for a persistent nonblocking issue; reserve a confirmation dialog for a decision that must precede the action.

components.title: Bottom sheet
jobs: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
useWhen: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
avoidWhen: Persistent wider-window secondary content or a small anchored choice fits another component.

adaptive.reason: Persistent secondary content fits beside the main task.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and modal bottom sheets.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.show()/showModal(); shared runtime handles dragging and dismissal.

components.title: Side sheet
jobs: Optional content and actions, without interrupting the main view.
useWhen: Optional content and actions, without interrupting the main view.
avoidWhen: The content is peer navigation or requires a blocking modal decision.

adaptive.reason: Secondary content must fit a compact window.
Use a dialog when a compact task must block progress.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and modal side sheets.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog and shared drag/dismiss behavior.

components.title: Floating sheet
jobs: Secondary content on a surface that floats free of every window edge.
useWhen: Detached secondary content or tools.
avoidWhen: Urgent decisions need dialogs; edge content needs sheets.

implementation.documentedSupport: Inset floating dialog surface.
implementation.webAdaptation: Shares Dialogs initialization; no edge attachment or drag handle.

materialGuidance.reason: Related guidance is not a dedicated component specification.

components.selectionExample: A required delete confirmation needs a dialog. Floating geometry alone does not make a secondary sheet the right decision prompt.

components.title: Drag handle
jobs: The bar that says a thing can be dragged — and nothing that does the dragging.
useWhen: The bar that says a thing can be dragged — and nothing that does the dragging.
avoidWhen: No pointer drag behavior and equivalent keyboard path are implemented by the containing component.

implementation.documentedSupport: Decorative grip and actionable button grip.
implementation.webAdaptation: The host element determines semantics; no general dragging engine.
limitations: A grip outside supported sheets does not implement dragging or its keyboard alternative.

upstreamReview.note: Optional drag handle is bottom sheet anatomy. Android handle supports accessible expand/collapse. This does not verify the generic vertical handle or ExpressiveCSS dismiss-on-tap behavior as an identical spec.

materialGuidance.reason: Related guidance is not a dedicated component specification.

components.title: Badges
jobs: Notifications, counts, or status on navigation items and icons.
useWhen: Attach counts or status to another item.
avoidWhen: Interactive filters need chips; messages need feedback.

implementation.documentedSupport: Small dot and large count badges.
implementation.webAdaptation: Expose counts through the enclosing control name when its icon is hidden.

components.selectionExample: An unread count belongs on the inbox icon as a badge. A selectable Unread filter needs a chip or selection control with its own name and state.

components.title: Tooltips
jobs: Material Design 3 tooltips, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 tooltips, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The icon already has visible text, or the tooltip would be the control’s only accessible name.

implementation.documentedSupport: Plain and rich tooltips; CSS child and runtime-generated forms.
implementation.webAdaptation: The selected form determines ownership; CSS-only hover/focus is not runtime initialization.

components.title: Snackbar
jobs: Material Design 3 snackbars, from the HTML.
useWhen: Brief, nonblocking feedback after an action.
avoidWhen: Persistent issues need banners; decisions need dialogs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Transient message with optional action and close control.
implementation.webAdaptation: Use the documented announcement and timeout behavior.

components.selectionExample: A successful save can use a snackbar. Offline status that still allows editing needs a persistent banner; a required irreversible-delete confirmation needs a dialog before the action.

components.title: Banners
jobs: A prominent message that stays put until the user deals with it.
useWhen: Persistent feedback while work can continue.
avoidWhen: Transient confirmation needs snackbar; blocking choices need dialog.

implementation.documentedSupport: Basic/rich and standard/vibrant; square basic banners.
implementation.webAdaptation: Persistent in-flow feedback; application owns dismissal.

materialGuidance.reason: Retained framework pattern absent from the reviewed current M3 component inventory; related current guidance does not certify this implementation.

components.selectionExample: A Saved message should not leave a permanent banner. Use a snackbar. A sync outage that permits local edits fits a banner; an unavoidable decision fits a dialog. This banner is a framework feedback pattern, not a verified current M3 component.

components.title: Progress indicators
jobs: Activity and progress. The HTML is the indicator.
useWhen: Measured progress or longer indeterminate waits.
avoidWhen: Brief unknown waits fit loading indicator; instant work needs none.

implementation.documentedSupport: Linear and circular progress, determinate and indeterminate.
implementation.webAdaptation: Prefer native progress where applicable; supply accessible state for custom hosts.

components.selectionExample: A two-second refresh with no measured fraction fits a loading indicator. An upload with bytes transferred needs determinate progress, even if short; a long job with no fraction can use indeterminate progress. Never invent a percentage. Indeterminate linear bars remain supported; the short-wait replacement specifically targets indeterminate circular spinners.

components.title: Loading indicator
jobs: A shape that morphs while it spins, for waits under five seconds.
useWhen: Brief waits under about five seconds, no known fraction.
avoidWhen: Measured or long-running work needs progress.

implementation.documentedSupport: Uncontained and contained morphing loading indicator.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only; the author supplies an accessible waiting message.

components.selectionExample: A file upload reporting 42% needs determinate progress, not the morphing loading shape. A longer unmeasured job needs indeterminate progress. Do not flash an indicator for an effectively instant response or announce a fabricated value.

components.title: Carousel
jobs: Material 3 adaptive carousels for visual collections.
useWhen: Browse a visual collection horizontally.
avoidWhen: Dense comparisons need lists; enlargement needs lightbox.

implementation.documentedSupport: Adaptive visual collections with documented layout variants.
implementation.webAdaptation: Runtime owns sizing and navigation; reduced motion removes parallax and morphing.

components.selectionExample: A transaction history must support scanning rows and values. Use a list instead of hiding records across carousel slides.

components.title: Lightbox
jobs: Lightbox for enlarge-on-click images.
useWhen: Enlarge an image on activation.
avoidWhen: Tasks need dialogs; browsing collections needs carousel.

implementation.documentedSupport: Enlarge-on-activation image and dismissal.
implementation.webAdaptation: ExpressiveCSS media behavior, not an upstream component contract.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A payment confirmation needs a dialog, even if its design contains an image. Lightbox is for inspecting enlarged media.

components.title: Toolbars
jobs: Frequently used actions for the current page.
useWhen: Group frequent actions near their content.
avoidWhen: Destinations need navigation; page identity needs app bar.

implementation.documentedSupport: Floating/docked, standard/vibrant, vertical floating, and companion FAB.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only commands; no automatic composite toolbar keyboard model.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile belong in navigation. A toolbar near a document can hold edit, share, and formatting actions.

components.title: Search
jobs: A search bar, and the view it expands into.
useWhen: A search bar, and the view it expands into.
avoidWhen: The field is ordinary data entry rather than finding content.

implementation.documentedSupport: Search bar and expanded search view.
implementation.webAdaptation: Application toggles hidden for docked views or opens a native dialog for full-screen views; optional Autocomplete owns suggestions.

components.title: Fieldsets
jobs: Grouped form sections, from the HTML.
useWhen: Name related form controls with a legend.
avoidWhen: Visual content grouping needs cards or sections.

implementation.documentedSupport: Outlined, filled, and rounded form groups.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native fieldset/legend; related text-field tokens do not make this an M3 component.

materialGuidance.reason: Related guidance is not a dedicated component specification.

components.selectionExample: A promotional feature block needs a section or card. Use a fieldset when a shared legend explains related inputs, such as delivery preferences.

components.title: Text fields
jobs: Material Design 3 text fields, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 text fields, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The value comes from a constrained set better represented by selection controls.

implementation.documentedSupport: Filled and outlined fields, supporting text, and error states.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native input/textarea with explicit label and description relationships.

components.title: Select
jobs: Choose one option, or several, from a styled menu.
useWhen: Choose one option, or several, from a styled menu.
avoidWhen: A short option set should remain visible or free-form entry is required.

implementation.documentedSupport: Single/multiple selection, optgroups, and browser-default fallback.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native select enhanced by runtime; this is related to menu/text-field patterns.

upstreamReview.note: Exposed dropdown is an official menu variant; editable variants accept typed input. Native select enhancement and multi-select are ExpressiveCSS adaptations.

materialGuidance.reason: Related guidance is not a dedicated component specification.

components.title: Checkboxes
jobs: Material Design 3 checkboxes, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 checkboxes, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The setting applies immediately or exactly one option must be chosen.

implementation.documentedSupport: Unchecked, checked, indeterminate, and disabled.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native checkbox; indeterminate is set through the DOM property.

components.title: Radio buttons
jobs: Material Design 3 radios, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 radios, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: Several choices may be selected or compact direct manipulation is better.

implementation.documentedSupport: Native radio groups and disabled controls.
implementation.webAdaptation: Shared name provides exclusivity; fieldset/legend names the group.

components.title: Switches
jobs: Material Design 3 switches, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 switches, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: A later Save action commits the choice.

implementation.documentedSupport: Native checkbox switches and disabled controls.
implementation.webAdaptation: Input state owns selection and form value.

components.title: Slider
jobs: Selections from a range of values.
useWhen: Adjust a bounded numeric range.
avoidWhen: Exact typed values need a numeric field.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard, centered, range, horizontal/vertical, and five sizes.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native range inputs with runtime value-label and range coordination.

components.selectionExample: An invoice amount needs a labeled number field with appropriate precision. A slider fits approximate volume or brightness adjustment.

components.title: Chips
jobs: Small blocks for contacts, tags, and filters.
useWhen: Compact filters, tags, or contextual actions.
avoidWhen: Passive counts need badges; primary actions need buttons.

implementation.documentedSupport: Assist, suggestion, filter, input, and display chips.
implementation.webAdaptation: Element choice defines behavior; display chips are a framework extension.

components.selectionExample: A passive unread count is a badge. Turning it into a filter chip falsely suggests a selectable state unless filtering is implemented.

components.title: Autocomplete
jobs: Suggest values under a text field as the user types.
useWhen: Suggest values under a text field as the user types.
avoidWhen: Suggestions are unavailable or the value must be limited to a small visible set.

implementation.documentedSupport: Single and multi-select suggestions.
implementation.webAdaptation: Runtime combobox behavior attached to a text field; no standalone upstream component claim.

upstreamReview.note: Exposed dropdown is an official menu variant; editable variants accept typed input. Native select enhancement and multi-select are ExpressiveCSS adaptations.

materialGuidance.reason: Related guidance is not a dedicated component specification.

components.title: Date picker
jobs: Select a date, a range, or several dates from a calendar.
useWhen: Choose dates or ranges in an inline calendar.
avoidWhen: Simple entry may use native date; time needs time input.

implementation.documentedSupport: Inline single-date, range, and multiple-date calendar.
implementation.webAdaptation: Inline adaptation; open()/close() are deprecated no-ops.
limitations: Modal picker parity is not provided by the documented inline API.

upstreamReview.note: destination and main heading verified; full guideline not reviewed; link-observed; full specifications not reviewed

components.selectionExample: A single date with no calendar-specific requirements can use a labeled native date input. Do not choose this picker expecting a popup: its calendar is inline and requires the documented visibility option.

components.title: Time picker
jobs: Pick a time from a clock face, in 12-hour or 24-hour form.
useWhen: Choose time in an inline clock.
avoidWhen: Simple entry may use native time; dates need date input.

implementation.documentedSupport: Inline clock and digital input; 12-hour and 24-hour formats.
implementation.webAdaptation: Inline adaptation; open()/close() are deprecated no-ops.
limitations: Modal picker parity is not provided by the documented inline API.

upstreamReview.note: destination and selected Guidelines tab verified; full guideline not reviewed; link-observed; full specifications not reviewed

components.selectionExample: An appointment time can use a labeled native time input when platform entry is enough. Do not choose this picker expecting a popup: its clock stays inline.

materialMappingPolicy.implementation: documentedSupport is a source-reviewed summary for frameworkVersion, not a complete variant inventory or a browser pass; guideSource identifies the owning contract section.
materialMappingPolicy.upstream: relationship identifies an upstream component (including explicitly marked legacy components), layout pattern, related guidance, or framework extension. upstreamReview states exactly which source and scope were reviewed; a link alone is not a specification review.
materialMappingPolicy.parity: Full upstream parity and browser conformance are not assessed by this mapping. Unlisted limitations are unknown, not evidence of completeness.
